questions.question: In high-performance out-of-order superscalar processors, what is the fundamental microarchitectural challenge known as 'memory disambiguation'?
options: Determining whether a younger load instruction accesses the same physical memory address as an older, pending store instruction whose target address is not yet resolved.
Resolving conflicts between instruction cache misses and data cache misses competing for the same interconnect port to main memory.
Distinguishing whether a virtual address references private thread-local storage or shared global memory within the operating system page tables.
Identifying whether a translation lookaside buffer (TLB) miss was caused by a page privilege fault or a physical page absence.
Arbitrating read and write priorities among simultaneously issued vector instructions accessing multi-bank register files.

questions.question: In invalidation-based snooping cache coherence protocols such as MESI, what is the primary operational advantage of providing an 'Exclusive' (E) state in addition to the 'Shared' (S) state?
options: It allows modified data to be written back to main memory asynchronously without locking the memory interconnect.
It enables a core to silently transition the cache line to Modified (M) on a subsequent write without broadcasting an invalidation request to the interconnect.
It bypasses the need for cache tags by keeping exclusive cache lines directly inside processor execution registers.
It permits multiple processor cores to simultaneously retain identical, read-only copies of a cache line without causing cache pollution.
It automatically flushes the cache line to the level-three (L3) shared cache whenever an interrupt service routine is invoked.

questions.question: In CMOS digital logic circuits, why is dynamic switching power dissipation fundamentally proportional to the square of the supply voltage (P_dynamic ∝ V_DD²)?
options: Because subthreshold leakage current exhibits an exponential dependence on V_DD, which simplifies to a quadratic relationship under typical operating temperatures.
Because the carrier drift velocity in short-channel MOSFETs saturates linearly with the electric field across the source and drain terminals.
Because charging a load capacitance C_L to V_DD requires the power supply to deliver an energy of E = C_L · V_DD² per switching transition, independent of channel resistance.
Because gate oxide capacitance increases proportionally with V_DD due to quantum-mechanical depletion effects in the polysilicon gate.
Because threshold voltage V_th decreases quadratically with increasing V_DD due to severe drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL).

questions.question: In ASIC physical design and Static Timing Analysis (STA), what is the core methodology of 'useful skew' (clock skew scheduling)?
options: Adding dummy flip-flops along high-fanout nets to artificially equalize clock tree branch depths and eliminate all clock skew across the die.
Dynamically modulating the system clock frequency during runtime to avoid setup timing violations caused by transient IR drops.
Modifying static data path logic cells into dynamic Domino gates to match clock propagation delays across different pipeline stages.
Intentionally delaying or advancing the clock arrival time at specific register clock pins to trade timing slack between adjacent pipeline stages.
Enforcing strictly identical wire lengths across all clock routing paths to ensure zero clock skew under worst-case process variation.

questions.question: In the design of a standard six-transistor (6T) SRAM cell, what transistor sizing requirement (the 'Cell Ratio') is critical to ensure read stability and prevent an accidental read upset?
options: The pull-up pMOS transistors must be significantly wider than the pull-down nMOS transistors to maintain high noise margins in standby mode.
The access nMOS transistors must be stronger than both the pull-up and pull-down transistors to rapidly discharge the high-capacitance bitline.
The pull-up pMOS transistors must be stronger than the access nMOS transistors so that the internal '0' storage node is clamped securely near ground.
The access nMOS transistors and pull-down nMOS transistors must be sized identically to ensure symmetrical read and write noise margins.
The pull-down nMOS transistors must be stronger than the access nMOS transistors to prevent the voltage at the internal '0' node from exceeding the trip point of the opposing inverter.
